As many as 392 civic officials across Madhya Pradesh face government action over alleged financial irregularities, and seven have been terminated from service so far, a senior official said on Sunday (October 25, 2026). The officials facing action include 135 chief municipal officers (CMOs).
Additional Chief Secretary (Housing and Urban Development) Sanjay Dubey explained how the government is using technology and artificial intelligence (AI) to detect irregularities and take action against those responsible. His remarks came days after a video of him highlighting a pattern of corruption in civic bodies at a meeting of officials surfaced. He also said more than 80 government contractors have also faced action for irregularities such as supplying items at inflated rates.
In the video, Mr. Dubey is heard telling municipal officials that the government was tracking their purchases to identify irregularities. He gave the example of two civic bodies, without naming them, one of which purchased a garbage-collection vehicle for ₹2 lakh, while the other bought the same vehicle for ₹6 lakh, citing the addition of four dustbins to the purchase.
Speaking to reporters, Mr. Dubey said the Department has also recovered around ₹3-4 crore from officials over excess payments, and that action is being taken continuously against those involved in irregularities. He said that action against 135 CMOs included demotion, withholding of increments, and dismissals, based on the scale of the irregularity or negligence.
“As of now, action has been taken or is being taken against 392 officers of different ranks, including 135 at the chief municipal officer level,” he said. Mr. Dubey said that the viral video was from a biannual training session of municipal commissioners, CMOs, civic engineers and other officials, organised to explain how the government is monitoring their work.
“We are expecting from them that they do not incur excess expenditure or do something that falls under irregularities, has an adverse impact on them and diminishes the government’s image,” he said.
Mr. Dubey said that the Department has been tracking expenditure by civic bodies from State government funds and their own budgets, as all purchases have to be mandatorily processed through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) portal, while the payment can be made only through the e-Nagar Palika portal.
“First, we check if the purchases are within their expenditure limits. We then track the purchases and payments made through the two portals and apply artificial intelligence to the data to do a rate comparison to find out the prices of the same items purchased by different civic bodies around the same time. We also analyse if a vendor is supplying the same items at different rates to different bodies,” Mr. Dubey said.
The government is also monitoring whether rules are being manipulated to favour particular contractors. “Sometimes a tender is awarded in parts to give it to a particular person,” he said. “We wouldn’t have gathered the information about their purchases with their own funds if we had not used technology,” he said.
Mr. Dubey said civic bodies across the State place around 1,000-1,500 small and large purchase orders every day. The information is presented during the training session to convey to officials that their activities are being regularly monitored. “Based on this, we train them against such irregularities,” he said.
